Extrapyramidal effects → acute dystonia within hours to days, treated with diphenhydramine or benztropine
Akathisia → restlessness mistaken for anxiety or undertreated nausea
Bowel sounds and distention before giving → never drive peristalsis against an obstruction
12-WEEK maximum duration
never: Parkinson disease → the disease is dopamine deficiency
quick.working: nausea and vomiting relieved, gastric stasis and reflux symptoms down

points: Nausea from gastroparesis or reflux, where the stomach isn't emptying.

(IV) facilitation of small bowel intubation in radiographic procedures
(unlabeled) hiccups

seizure disorders → lowers the seizure threshold
hypertension

history of tardive dyskinesia

moderate or severe renal or hepatic impairment (intranasal)

nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) NMS from dopamine blockade; lead-pipe rigidity and hyporeflexia distinguish it from serotonin syndrome

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for signs of depression periodically
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) depression; dopamine blockade can produce or worsen it, including suicidal ideation

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for hyperprolactinemia → menstrual abnormalities, galactorrhea, gynecomastia, sexual dysfunction

nursing_interventions.action: Limit therapy to 12 weeks unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk

nursing_interventions.action: Give 30 min before meals and at bedtime (gastroparesis/reflux)

Rash → SJS/TEN

nursing_interventions.action: Check K⁺ and Mg²⁺ before IV administration in at-risk patients

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for extrapyramidal effects → involuntary movements, facial grimacing, rigidity, shuffling gait, hand tremor
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) extrapyramidal reactions; uncommon with ondansetron, far more likely with metoclopramide or prochlorperazine

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for rash
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Derm) SJS/TEN; a new rash with mucosal involvement or blistering means stop the drug now

nursing_interventions.action: Give IV over at least 2-5 min, not as a rapid push

Fall risk → sedation plus orthostasis together

Tardive dyskinesia → assess q2mo and for 8-12 wk after stopping
CBC → agranulocytosis; a sore throat and fever here means a CBC, not a cold
(IV) Dilute and give slowly; stop for burning or pain
never: Elderly with dementia-related psychosis → ↑ mortality, the black box
quick.working: nausea and vomiting relieved, patient tolerating PO intake

secondary: Tx of schizophrenia
short-term Tx of non-psychotic anxiety
(unlabeled) migraine, intractable hiccups, vertigo

action: alters the effects of dopamine in the CNS → blocks D2 receptors

severe liver or cardiovascular disease
concurrent use of large doses of other CNS depressants
children <2 yr or <9 kg, and children undergoing surgery (per the label)

nursing_interventions.rationale: → alpha blockade causes orthostatic hypotension, which only shows up on a positional set of vitals; the drug may also cause Q-wave and T-wave changes and prolong QT

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for akathisia (restlessness, an inner drive to keep moving) and extrapyramidal effects → parkinsonian (masklike face, shuffling gait, rigidity, tremor) and dystonic (muscle spasms, twisting, twitching)
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) extrapyramidal reactions from D2 blockade. Akathisia is routinely mistaken for anxiety or undertreated nausea, and giving more drug makes it worse

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for tardive dyskinesia → rhythmic uncontrolled movements of the mouth, face, tongue, and extremities; assess q2mo during therapy and 8-12 wk after discontinuation → report immediately, it may be irreversible

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for neuroleptic malignant syndrome → fever, severe muscle rigidity, tachycardia, diaphoresis, labile BP, altered consciousness → notify the provider immediately
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) NMS; mortality is significant and the treatment is stopping the drug plus supportive cooling

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor CBC with differential periodically

nursing_interventions.rationale: → (EENT, GI) anticholinergic activity; older adults are far more sensitive and can become delirious

working_because: patient able to tolerate PO intake
black_box: ↑ mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis → antipsychotics are not approved for dementia-related psychosis
medications.antidote: diphenhydramine or benztropine for acute dystonic reactions

it works in the gut lumen, not in the blood → which is why it only works if it is in the stomach at the same time as the food

renal calculi
ventricular fibrillation
concurrent use of other calcium supplements → additive calcium load
hypophosphatemia

nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) the behavioral side effects are the signature problem with this drug and the most common reason it gets changed

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for rash → SJS and DRESS (fever, malaise, blisters, oral lesions, facial swelling, lymphadenopathy)
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Derm) DRESS appears 2-8 wk in and can look like a viral illness; the eosinophilia and organ involvement are what distinguish it. Any rash with mucosal lesions or blistering means stop now

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for anaphylaxis → dyspnea, wheezing, facial swelling → discontinue
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Misc) HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor CBC
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Hemat) AGRANULOCYTOSIS, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia

nursing_interventions.action: Assess renal function and adjust dose for impairment
nursing_interventions.rationale: → almost entirely renally excreted; in renal impairment the drug accumulates → sedation and ataxia at a normal dose

nursing_interventions.action: (Education) Never stop abruptly → always taper
nursing_interventions.rationale: abrupt withdrawal of any anticonvulsant risks withdrawal seizures and status epilepticus

footnotes: ⚠ Keppra is the easy one pharmacokinetically and the hard one behaviorally. If a question gives you a patient who became aggressive or depressed after starting an anticonvulsant, this is the drug.

highlight.headline: Stops seizures; IV loading for status
highlight.critical: IV ≤50 mg/min, NEVER in D5W

quick.one_liner: Blocks sodium channels → limits seizure spread. Saturable metabolism means a small dose change makes a large level change, so it needs levels.
watch: Serum level 10-20 mcg/mL → toxicity in a fixed order: NYSTAGMUS first, then ataxia, then confusion
(IV) No faster than 50 mg/min, NEVER in D5W → it precipitates; use saline with a filter
(IV) Continuous BP, ECG, and respiratory monitoring → hypotension and arrest are RATE-dependent
(IV) The site constantly → purple glove syndrome, which can progress to limb ischemia
Rash → SJS/TEN; phenytoin is one of the highest-risk drugs
Albumin → it's 90% protein-bound, so a 'normal' total level can be toxic when albumin is low
Hold tube feeds 1-2 hr before and after a PO dose → feeds bind it and drop the level
Gingival hyperplasia → meticulous oral care
quick.working: seizures diminished, level 10-20 with no nystagmus or ataxia

why_this_one.text: Status epilepticus and IV loading, fast and effective. Levels to follow and a hard IV rate limit. A small dose change can send the level far higher.
points: Status epilepticus and IV loading, fast and effective.
Levels to follow and a hard IV rate limit.
A small dose change can send the level far higher.

use.primary: Tx and prophylaxis of tonic-clonic (grand mal) seizures and complex partial seizures
secondary: status epilepticus after a benzodiazepine → IV loading
(antiarrhythmic) ventricular arrhythmias, particularly digoxin-induced

action: limits seizure propagation by altering ion transport → blocks voltage-gated Na⁺ channels in their inactivated state, so a neuron firing repetitively can't keep firing
may ↓ synaptic transmission
antiarrhythmic → shortens the action potential and ↓ automaticity in ventricular tissue
saturable (zero-order) metabolism → once the enzymes are saturated, a small ↑ in dose produces a large, disproportionate jump in serum level. That is why this drug needs levels and the others don't
contraindications: hypersensitivity; hypersensitivity to propylene glycol (injection only)
history of phenytoin-related hepatotoxicity
alcohol intolerance (injection and liquid only)
(injection) sinus bradycardia, SA block, 2nd- or 3rd-degree heart block, Stokes-Adams syndrome → the drug slows cardiac conduction

side_effects.note: almost entirely a function of IV infusion RATE, not dose
nystagmus is the EARLIEST sign of toxicity
gingival hyperplasia is the classic long-term effect: up to 50% of patients

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor serum phenytoin levels; therapeutic range 10-20 mcg/mL
nursing_interventions.rationale: → saturable metabolism means the level and the dose are not proportional. Toxicity appears in a fixed order: nystagmus first (~20), then ataxia (~30), then confusion and lethargy (~40+). That sequence is the exam question

nursing_interventions.action: (IV) Infuse no faster than 50 mg/min, and never in D5W
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (CV) CARDIAC ARREST and hypotension are RATE-dependent, not dose-dependent. Phenytoin precipitates in dextrose → use normal saline only, with an inline filter

nursing_interventions.action: (IV) Monitor BP, ECG, and respiratory function continuously during and after infusion
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (CV) hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmias; the propylene glycol diluent is itself cardiotoxic

nursing_interventions.action: (IV) Use a large-bore patent line and assess the site constantly → stop for any pain, burning, or discoloration
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Local) purple glove syndrome: progressive discoloration and edema distal to the site that can progress to limb ischemia. Highly alkaline drug

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for skin rash → DRESS, SJS, TEN; discontinue immediately
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Derm) phenytoin is one of the highest-risk drugs for SJS/TEN, especially in patients carrying HLA-B*15:02

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for phenytoin hypersensitivity syndrome → fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, angioedema
nursing_interventions.rationale: → may cause renal failure, RHABDOMYOLYSIS, and hepatic necrosis, and may be fatal. It appears 1-8 wk into therapy

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor notable changes in behavior indicating emergence or worsening of suicidal thoughts, behavior, or depression
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) SUICIDAL THOUGHTS; anticonvulsant class effect

nursing_interventions.action: (Seizures) Assess location, duration, and characteristics of seizure activity
nursing_interventions.rationale: the therapeutic endpoint

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor CBC, hepatic panel, and albumin
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Hemat) AGRANULOCYTOSIS and APLASTIC ANEMIA; phenytoin is highly protein-bound, so low albumin means a normal TOTAL level can still be a toxic FREE level

nursing_interventions.action: (Education) Meticulous oral hygiene and regular dental visits
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (GI) gingival hyperplasia; good oral care genuinely reduces its severity

nursing_interventions.action: (Education) Never stop abruptly → always taper
nursing_interventions.rationale: withdrawal seizures and status epilepticus

nursing_interventions.action: Hold enteral feedings 1-2 hr before and after a PO dose
nursing_interventions.rationale: tube feeds bind phenytoin and can drop the level into the subtherapeutic range → breakthrough seizures

working_because: serum level within 10-20 mcg/mL with no signs of toxicity
footnotes: ⚠ The highest-yield phenytoin facts, in order: levels 10-20; nystagmus is the first sign of toxicity; IV ≤50 mg/min; never in D5W; gingival hyperplasia long-term.
⚠ Low albumin changes the interpretation of the level. Phenytoin is ~90% protein-bound, so in hypoalbuminemia the free (active) fraction rises and a 'normal' total level can be toxic.

highlight.headline: Stops seizures; prevents migraine
highlight.critical: Sudden eye pain → acute angle-closure glaucoma

quick.one_liner: Sodium channel blockade, GABA enhancement, and glutamate blockade at once, plus weak carbonic anhydrase inhibition, which causes three of its side effects.
watch: Sudden eye pain or blurred vision, especially in the first month → ACUTE ANGLE-CLOSURE GLAUCOMA, an ophthalmic emergency
Push fluids → carbonic anhydrase inhibition causes kidney stones
↓ Sweating and temperature, especially in children and heat → oligohidrosis, then hyperthermia
Serum bicarbonate → metabolic acidosis
Cognitive slowing and word-finding difficulty → the reason patients call it 'Dopamax'
Suicidality
Weight loss
quick.working: seizures down, or migraines fewer and less severe

why_this_one.text: Seizures plus migraine prophylaxis in one drug, or when weight loss is welcome. Cognitive slowing is the reason patients stop.
points: Seizures plus migraine prophylaxis in one drug, or when weight loss is welcome.
Cognitive slowing is the reason patients stop.

use.primary: Tx of partial-onset seizures and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures → monotherapy or adjunct
secondary: prophylaxis of migraine
adjunct Tx of seizures in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome
(unlabeled) adjunct in bipolar disorder; infantile spasms

action: inhibits voltage-gated Na⁺ channels in neurons → fewer repetitive action potentials
enhances GABA, the main inhibitory neurotransmitter → more inhibition
prevents activation of excitatory (AMPA/kainate glutamate) receptors → less excitation
weak carbonic anhydrase inhibition → this one mechanism accounts for three of its side effects at once: metabolic acidosis, kidney stones, and ↓ sweating
contraindications: hypersensitivity
recent alcohol use (within 6 hr before or after, for XR forms)
metabolic acidosis
use cautiously in renal impairment and nephrolithiasis history

side_effects.note: the cognitive slowing is so characteristic patients call the drug 'Dopamax'

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for notable behavior changes indicating emergence or worsening of suicidal thoughts, behavior, or depression
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) SUICIDAL THOUGHTS/BEHAVIORS; a class effect of anticonvulsants

nursing_interventions.action: (Seizures) Assess location, duration, and characteristics of seizure activity
nursing_interventions.rationale: the therapeutic endpoint

nursing_interventions.action: (Migraine) Assess pain location, intensity, duration, and associated symptoms
nursing_interventions.rationale: topiramate is for migraine PREVENTION, not an acute attack → the endpoint is fewer headaches per month, not relief now

nursing_interventions.action: (Bipolar disorder) Assess mental status and cognitive abilities
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) cognitive slowing and memory impairment can be mistaken for the illness worsening

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for acute angle-closure glaucoma → sudden eye pain, blurred vision, ↓ visual acuity, especially in the first month
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (EENT) this is an ophthalmic EMERGENCY and can cause permanent vision loss. It happens early; a patient reporting new eye pain on topiramate needs to be seen immediately

nursing_interventions.action: (Education) Push fluids
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (GU) nephrolithiasis. Carbonic anhydrase inhibition alkalinizes urine and ↓ citrate → calcium phosphate stones form. Dilute urine is the defense

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for ↓ sweating and monitor temperature, especially in children and hot environments
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Derm) oligohidrosis → (Metabolic) hyperthermia. Carbonic anhydrase inhibition impairs sweating, and sweating is the body's main cooling route

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor serum bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Metabolic) carbonic anhydrase inhibition causes a non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis; symptoms are fatigue, anorexia, and hyperventilation

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor hepatic panel and CBC
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Hemat) BLEEDING and hepatic metabolism

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor weight
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (GI) weight loss is predictable and dose-related

nursing_interventions.action: (Education) Never stop abruptly → risk of status epilepticus; always taper
nursing_interventions.rationale: abrupt withdrawal of any anticonvulsant precipitates seizures

footnotes: ⚠ Three side effects, one mechanism: kidney stones, ↓ sweating, and metabolic acidosis all come from weak carbonic anhydrase inhibition. Learn the mechanism and you get all three for free.
⚠ Avoid in pregnancy: the ranking in this section is Depakote worst, then Topamax and Dilantin.

highlight.headline: Stops seizures; treats mania
highlight.critical: Three black boxes: liver, pancreas, fetus

quick.one_liner: Raises GABA, blocks sodium and T-type calcium channels → the broadest-spectrum one, which is why it covers absence seizures and bipolar mania too. Three black boxes.
watch: LIVER → malaise, weakness, lethargy, facial edema, anorexia, vomiting; LFTs at baseline and often in the first 6 months. The vague 'feeling unwell' prodrome is how you catch it, not the labs
PANCREAS → abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting; can be hemorrhagic and fatal, at any point in therapy
FETUS → verify pregnancy status and contraception; the most teratogenic anticonvulsant here
Serum ammonia if lethargic or confused → hyperammonemia can occur with normal LFTs and a therapeutic level
CBC with platelets → thrombocytopenia
Level 50-100 mcg/mL
Rash → DRESS
quick.working: seizures suppressed, mania or migraines down, level 50-100 with normal LFTs and platelets

why_this_one.text: Absence seizures, several seizure types at once, or bipolar mania → the broadest spectrum here. Three black boxes and the worst teratogen of the group.
points: Absence seizures, several seizure types at once, or bipolar mania → the broadest spectrum here.
Three black boxes and the worst teratogen of the group.

use.primary: monotherapy and supplemental Tx of simple and complex absence seizures, and of complex partial seizures
secondary: adjunct Tx in Pts. with multiple seizure types
(divalproex only) Tx of manic episodes in bipolar disorder
(divalproex only) prophylaxis of migraine

action: ↑ levels of GABA, the main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the CNS → more inhibition
blocks voltage-gated Na⁺ channels → fewer repetitive discharges
also blocks T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons → that is specifically why it works for absence seizures, which are generated by thalamocortical circuits
the broad mechanism is why it covers multiple seizure types at once, and why it is also a mood stabilizer
contraindications: hypersensitivity
hepatic impairment or significant hepatic disease
urea cycle disorders → risk of fatal hyperammonemic encephalopathy
BLACK BOX: mitochondrial disorders caused by POLG mutations → risk of fatal hepatotoxicity; includes children <2 yr with a suspected POLG disorder
BLACK BOX (OB/Rep): pregnancy, and women of reproductive potential not using effective contraception → absolutely contraindicated for migraine prophylaxis in pregnancy

nursing_interventions.action: (Seizures) Assess location, duration, and characteristics of seizure activity
nursing_interventions.rationale: the therapeutic endpoint

nursing_interventions.action: (Bipolar disorder) Assess mental status and cognitive abilities
nursing_interventions.rationale: the endpoint for the mania indication

nursing_interventions.action: (Migraine prophylaxis) Monitor frequency and intensity of migraine headaches
nursing_interventions.rationale: this is prevention, not acute treatment → fewer headaches per month is the measure

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for S/S of hepatotoxicity → malaise, weakness, lethargy, facial edema, anorexia, vomiting; check hepatic panel at baseline and frequently in the first 6 mo
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (GI) HEPATOTOXICITY and the first black box. Risk is highest in the first 6 months and in children <2 yr. The nonspecific 'feeling unwell' prodrome is what you actually catch it by, not the labs

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for S/S of pancreatitis → abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, anorexia; check amylase and lipase if suspected
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (GI) PANCREATITIS and the second black box. It can be hemorrhagic, rapid, and fatal, and can occur at any point in therapy

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor serum ammonia if the patient becomes lethargic, confused, or vomits unexplainedly
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Metabolic) HYPERAMMONEMIA can occur with a normal hepatic panel and a therapeutic valproate level; it presents as encephalopathy

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor CBC with platelets and assess for bruising and bleeding
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Hemat) thrombocytopenia is dose-related; check before surgery

nursing_interventions.action: Assess suicidal tendencies, ↑ risk in Pts. ≤24 yr
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) SUICIDAL THOUGHTS; anticonvulsant class effect

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for skin rash → DRESS; discontinue immediately
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Derm) DRESS, SJS, TEN

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor serum valproate levels (50-100 mcg/mL)
nursing_interventions.rationale: one of only two drugs in this section with a level to follow; confirms adherence and guides dosing

nursing_interventions.action: Verify pregnancy status and effective contraception in anyone of reproductive potential
nursing_interventions.rationale: → the third black box. Valproate causes neural tube defects and ↓ IQ in exposed children; it is the most teratogenic anticonvulsant in this section

nursing_interventions.action: (Education) Never stop abruptly → always taper
nursing_interventions.rationale: withdrawal seizures and status epilepticus

working_because: serum level 50-100 mcg/mL with normal LFTs and platelets
black_box: hepatotoxicity → including fatal hepatic failure, especially in children <2 yr and in POLG mitochondrial disorders; highest risk in the first 6 months
pancreatitis → cases have been hemorrhagic with rapid progression to death
fetal risk → neural tube defects and ↓ IQ; contraindicated for migraine prophylaxis in pregnancy
medications.antidote: L-carnitine for valproate-induced hyperammonemia
footnotes: ⚠ Three black boxes, three organs: liver, pancreas, fetus. That is the mnemonic for this drug.
⚠ Name trap: Depakote is divalproex sodium, Depakene is valproic acid, Depacon is IV. Only divalproex carries the bipolar mania and migraine indications.
⚠ Worst anticonvulsant in pregnancy, by a wide margin.

highlight.headline: Corrects metabolic acidosis
highlight.critical: It MOVES potassium into cells, it does not remove it

quick.one_liner: Alkalinizing agent → buffers acid to raise pH. Treats metabolic acidosis, traps drugs in alkaline urine, and temporarily shifts potassium into cells.
watch: It MOVES potassium into cells, it does not remove it → the K⁺ comes back; only dialysis, a binder, or a diuretic removes it
Fluid overload → every dose is a sodium load; I&O, daily weight, lung sounds
Overshooting into alkalosis → confusion, paresthesia, tetany
Ionized calcium → rising pH ↑ calcium binding to albumin → tetany
ABGs and electrolytes
(IV) The site → highly alkaline, causes tissue necrosis if it infiltrates
never: Same line as calcium-containing solutions → precipitation
quick.working: pH and bicarbonate rising toward normal, acidosis improving, K⁺ falling (hyperkalemia use)

why_this_one.text: Metabolic acidosis, urinary alkalinization in an overdose, or hyperkalemia that needs a temporary shift. Every dose is a sodium load.
points: Metabolic acidosis, urinary alkalinization in an overdose, or hyperkalemia that needs a temporary shift.
Every dose is a sodium load.

use.primary: Tx of metabolic acidosis
secondary: alkalinization of urine → ↑ excretion of certain drugs in overdose (salicylates, tricyclics)
antacid → relief of heartburn and indigestion
(unlabeled) stabilization of acid-base status in cardiac arrest
(unlabeled) Tx of life-threatening hyperkalemia → the alkalosis drives K⁺ into cells

action: releases bicarbonate ions → buffers excess hydrogen ion → ↑ serum pH, correcting metabolic acidosis

bicarbonate filtered into the urine raises urine pH → weak acids like salicylate become ionized and can't be reabsorbed → trapped and excreted (ion trapping, the same principle as lactulose in the colon)
neutralizes gastric acid directly → antacid effect
raising serum pH shifts K⁺ from the extracellular into the intracellular space → temporarily lowers serum potassium. It moves potassium, it does not remove it
contraindications: metabolic or respiratory alkalosis → you would be worsening the problem
hypocalcemia → alkalosis ↑ calcium binding to albumin, dropping ionized calcium further → tetany
hypernatremia → each dose is a sodium load
excessive chloride loss
Pts. on sodium-restricted diets (HF, hypertension, renal failure, cirrhosis)
renal failure → cannot handle the sodium or the bicarbonate load
severe abdominal pain of unknown cause → could be an acute abdomen

side_effects.note: from the sodium load

effects: gastric rupture (rare, with large PO doses)

nursing_interventions.action: Assess fluid balance throughout therapy → I&O, daily weight, edema, lung sounds, JVD
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (CV) each dose is a sodium load, and sodium brings water. Report S/S of fluid overload: hypertension, edema, dyspnea, rales/crackles, frothy sputum

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for alkalosis → confusion, irritability, paresthesia, tetany, altered breathing pattern
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (F&E) metabolic alkalosis. You can overshoot the acidosis you're treating, and the symptoms of alkalosis come from the ionized calcium falling as pH rises

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for hypernatremia → edema, weight gain, hypertension, tachycardia, fever, flushed skin, mental irritability, thirst
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (F&E) hypernatremia from the sodium load

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for hypokalemia → weakness, fatigue, U wave on ECG, arrhythmias, polyuria, polydipsia
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (F&E) raising pH shifts K⁺ into cells. In a patient treated for hyperkalemia this is the intended effect; in anyone else it is an adverse one

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor ABGs, serum electrolytes, and serum calcium
nursing_interventions.rationale: → pH and bicarbonate guide the dose; the sodium, potassium, and calcium are the collateral damage

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for signs of hypocalcemia → perioral numbness, paresthesias, Trousseau and Chvostek signs, tetany
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (F&E) alkalosis ↑ calcium binding to albumin → ionized calcium falls even when total calcium is unchanged

nursing_interventions.action: (IV) Assess the site frequently; avoid extravasation
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Local) sodium bicarbonate is highly alkaline and hypertonic → tissue necrosis if it infiltrates

nursing_interventions.action: (Antacid) Assess for epigastric or abdominal pain and for frank or occult blood in stool, emesis, or gastric aspirate
nursing_interventions.rationale: → distinguishes simple dyspepsia from GI bleeding or cardiac pain, where an antacid wastes time

nursing_interventions.action: Do not give in the same line as calcium-containing solutions
nursing_interventions.rationale: calcium carbonate precipitates → occluded line and particulate embolism risk

working_because: ↑ in urinary pH and clinical improvement of acidosis → serum pH and bicarbonate rising toward normal
enhanced excretion of selected overdoses and poisonings
footnotes: ⚠ Sodium bicarbonate for hyperkalemia MOVES potassium into cells; it does not remove it from the body. The potassium comes back out. Only dialysis, a GI binder, or a diuretic actually removes it. Exam questions live on this distinction.
⚠ Every dose is a sodium load. In HF, renal failure, or cirrhosis that is the limiting factor, not the pH.

highlight.headline: Stops bleeding
highlight.critical: It protects clot → thrombosis is the risk

quick.one_liner: Antifibrinolytic → blocks plasminogen from becoming plasmin, so a clot that formed is not dissolved. The exact opposite of a blood thinner.
watch: Thrombosis → unilateral leg swelling, dyspnea and chest pain, new focal neuro deficit; you've switched off clot breakdown
Screen for thrombosis history and hormonal contraception use BEFORE the first dose → both are contraindications and both are easy to miss
Color vision with prolonged use → the earliest sign of retinal toxicity
Menstrual flow → pad counts, not 'better'
H&H
quick.working: menstrual blood loss reduced, H&H stabilizing, no thrombotic event

why_this_one.text: Bleeding you need to stop → heavy menstrual bleeding, trauma hemorrhage, surgical bleeding. The opposite of everything in Blood Thinners.
points: Bleeding you need to stop → heavy menstrual bleeding, trauma hemorrhage, surgical bleeding.
The opposite of everything in Blood Thinners.

use.primary: (PO) Tx of cyclic heavy menstrual bleeding
secondary: (IV) short-term prevention of bleeding in hemophilia patients undergoing tooth extraction
(IV, unlabeled) trauma hemorrhage, surgical bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage

action: binds the lysine-binding sites on plasminogen → blocks plasminogen from attaching to fibrin → it never converts to plasmin
plasmin is the enzyme that dissolves clots, so without it the clot that formed stays formed
this is the mirror image of everything in the Blood Thinners section: those drugs prevent clots, this one protects them
it does not create a clot → it preserves one. In a patient with nothing to stabilize, it does nothing
contraindications: hypersensitivity
active thromboembolic disease or a history of thrombosis → you are removing the body's clot-dissolving system
acquired defective color vision (IV) → ocular toxicity is monitored by color vision, so you lose the ability to detect it
subarachnoid hemorrhage → risk of cerebral ischemia from unopposed clot
concurrent use of combination hormonal contraception (PO) → both are prothrombotic; together the thrombosis risk is additive

side_effects.note: the predictable consequence of the mechanism
seizures are dose-related and mostly an IV/cardiac-surgery phenomenon

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor menstrual flow before and during therapy → pad or tampon counts, clot size, duration of bleeding
nursing_interventions.rationale: → the therapeutic endpoint; a countable measure beats 'heavy' or 'better'

nursing_interventions.action: Assess for S/S of thrombosis → unilateral leg swelling, calf pain and warmth (DVT); dyspnea, chest pain, tachycardia (PE); focal neuro deficit (stroke); chest pain (MI)
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (CV) thrombosis. You have switched off fibrinolysis, so any clot that forms is not getting cleared

nursing_interventions.action: Screen for personal or family history of thrombosis and for use of combination hormonal contraception before the first dose
nursing_interventions.rationale: → both are contraindications and both are easy to miss on a med reconciliation

nursing_interventions.action: Refer for ophthalmologic examination if therapy continues for several days or longer
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (EENT) altered color vision is the earliest sign of retinal toxicity; it is detectable before the patient notices it

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for seizure activity, particularly with IV dosing
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Neuro) SEIZURES; dose-related and reported mainly after high-dose IV use in cardiac surgery

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor hemoglobin and hematocrit
nursing_interventions.rationale: → confirms the bleeding is actually being controlled, rather than just appearing lighter

nursing_interventions.action: Monitor for anaphylaxis with PO dosing
nursing_interventions.rationale: → (Misc) ANAPHYLAXIS

working_because: reduced menstrual blood loss → fewer pads/tampons, shorter duration, smaller clots
hemoglobin and hematocrit stabilizing or rising
footnotes: ⚠ Tranexamic acid is the opposite of every drug in the Blood Thinners section. Anticoagulants and antiplatelets stop clots from forming; this one stops clots from dissolving. Which means every contraindication is a situation where a clot would be dangerous.
⚠ Oral contraceptive plus tranexamic acid is the interaction to catch: exactly the patient population being treated for heavy menstrual bleeding.
